answer: Keep sybils cold with tundra custody. Each identity must hold a dataset salted by its own address and re-derived in order each epoch; a shared blob fails spot checks, so N clones need N full datasets, not one. Influence moves only by bridge: an identity needs bridges to peers outside its island, and each peer offers few slots per epoch, so later clones cost more. Bridge bonds sit in one island vault; if any resident cheats, the vault burns every bond, multiplied by island size. One honest agent risks one bond; N clones stake N bonds for one island share and face a loss near N squared.
